sections.heading: Common constraints
sections.markdown: `go` accepts a call expression and yields `Task<T, E>`, with E from the declared error signature and default Never. Arguments, captures and complete outcomes must be Sendable; ordinary outer var capture is forbidden. Pass copyable local values explicitly; noncopyable resources use consuming parameters. await t propagates only E (no try when E is Never); awaiting a task that ended Cancelled makes the waiter itself enter uncatchable cancellation unwinding, so cancellation propagates up the chain of waiters. Channel.send on a closed channel panics with E0702. Task.all/first/firstSuccess accept homogeneous `Array<Task<T, E>>` and are suspending functions without await prefixes. A scope owns child cancellation and failure propagation; go outside a scope is independent. Once an outcome is selected, Task.first/firstSuccess and the failure branch of Task.all request cancellation before returning and do not wait for remaining cleanup. Tasks keep their original executor/scope ownership; scope exit still waits for every member to terminate and finish cleanup. Early aggregate return does not discard later failures or promise early external program completion.

sections.heading: Task handle
sections.markdown: poll() returns `TaskResult<T, E>?`; null means unfinished. awaitResult() reports one of Success(T), Error(E), Panic(PanicInfo), Cancelled. Payload type notation does not define field names. T, E and the entire owned PanicInfo graph must be copyable and Sendable. Repeated observation preserves the task terminal outcome and returns independent logical snapshots. Cancellation is checked only at suspension points and cannot be caught by the cancelled task; a waiter that uses await or an aggregate function is cancelled as well, while awaitResult() and poll() report the Cancelled value without propagating it.

sections.heading: scope — structured concurrency
sections.markdown: Default scope cancels siblings on child failure; isolated scope lets them continue. Both drain all members before exit, give panic priority on its independent channel, and never put panic in TaskFailures<E>. Let B be escaping body business errors and E direct-child declared errors. Default scope exposes B | E; isolated exposes B | TaskFailures<E>, with no child aggregate channel when E=Never. Both need no scope marker when B and E are Never. try scope marks exit propagation, not calls in its body; real try-body protection or individual call markers remain required. Abrupt body exit cancels and drains both forms, retaining owned pending control transfers and valid body lifetimes. Isolated body errors propagate directly before child business aggregates. Parent cancellation already entered at a legal checkpoint remains uncatchable. These target semantics still need compiler/runtime qualification; see spec 10.7.

sections.heading: Task.yieldNow() vs yield expr — two different suspensions
sections.markdown:
`yield expr` delivers one owned element and parks its independent producer frame; `yield ()` is a real Unit element, never EOS. `Task.yieldNow()` produces no element and returns the activation to its executor queue. Consumption may wait through the producer, so `hasNext()` and `next()` cannot promise `no_suspend`. Creating the lazy Iterator executes no body and has no immediate producer throw.

Repeated `hasNext()` preserves a cached yield without advancing; `next()` transfers its owner once. Exhaustion is reported by false from `hasNext()` and E0432 from an exhausted `next()`. One Iterator accepts one consumer at a time. Consumer cancellation and early abandonment close the producer and run registered unfinished cleanup exactly once. An unstarted producer has registered no defer. Drop only signals close, and the original executor drains it before Instance code retirement.

The Checked development subset and its unqualified waits, borrow environments, for-in, Channel and platform paths are listed in spec §17.39. This does not claim complete Generator, scheduler or async-stream qualification. The old analyzer generator-scheduling and defer bans (E0385/E0386) are historical diagnostics, not the current Checked rules.
